proof:
The contracted body $B_t=q+(1-vt)(B-q)$ is nested in $B$, so midpoint compatibility persists. The convex hull of the three lifted bodies has exactly these integer fibers, because at base zero a convex combination uses equal total weights from the two endpoints, and at either extreme base it uses only that fiber. The new support is $h_i-tv e_i$, where $e_i=h_i-v_i\cdot q\ge0$. Thus at middle level $s$ the supporting $B_t$ trace contributes zero volume and the $A_t$ threshold increases by $tv e_i$.

Normalized section areas of $A_t$ at levels tending to the old proper level $2s_i^0-h_i$ converge to $\sigma_i$. After translating parallel planes, compactness gives upper Hausdorff inclusion. For lower inclusion, each point of the limiting section is approximated from both sides by mixing it slightly with fixed interior points above and below the level. The mixed points are interior to $A$ and eventually lie in $A_t$, by support-function convergence and their positive distance from the boundary. Their connecting segments supply nearby points on the moving sections. Compactness of the limiting section gives the lower Hausdorff inclusion, and volume continuity for convex sections gives convergence of the coarea. In $d=1$ the proper sections are singletons with counting measure one. Fubini then shows that the extra threshold shift changes the budget by $-tv\sigma_i e_i+o(t)$, uniformly for $|s-s_i^0|=O(t)$.

For $s$ near $s_i^0$ the new row budget is continuous and strictly decreasing. Its decrease per unit increase in $s$ is bounded below by a positive constant from an interior ball around $y_0$ contained in every small $K_t$, and above by parallel section bounds in common enclosing balls. The symmetric differences and the support shift make its uniform difference from the old budget $O(t)$. Invert each row locally in $s$ for a common mass near $Q$. The sum of inverse levels is strictly decreasing, has opposite signs at two fixed nearby levels on opposite sides of $Q$, and changes by $O(t)$ at $Q$. The two slope bounds imply that its unique zero occurs at $Q_t=Q+O(t)$ and that all corresponding levels are $s_i^0+O(t)$. They sum to zero and determine a unique $y_t=y_0+O(t)$ by the spanning and balance of the normals. This point is interior to $K_t$ for small $t$.

Write the first-order expansion of each row at $s=v_i\cdot y_t$, multiply by $\lambda_i$ and sum. The source displacement term vanishes because $\sum_i v_i=0$, giving $Q_t=Q+t(q_{\rm shape}-vJ(q))+o(t)$. Substituting back into each row gives convergence of the corresponding projected difference quotient to the displayed velocity coordinate. The projection map is invertible onto the sum-zero space, so the right derivative of the point exists. The same balance makes the new middle traces cover the whole middle plane, hence this common mass is a pointwise upper bound. Both endpoints are exposed and have exactly their ordinary raw depths by 2acc8bc803acf1c0. The $B$ maximum scales homothetically. For the $A_t$ maximum, every halfspace measure changes by at most $|A_t\mathbin{\triangle}A|$. Old depth can be extended by zero outside $A$ by separation, so taking the supremum over all continuous points gives $m(A_t)\le m_A+O(t)$. This handles new endpoint points. The expansion of $|B_t|=(1-vt)^d b$ gives the asserted total derivative. Dividing the two active bounds by the total and using $Q=rM$ gives the displayed normalized derivatives. If both are strictly negative, the gapped branch remains below $r$ and so does the actual normalized global maximum for all sufficiently small positive $t$.

The endpoint inequality is $D+dv(a+k)>0$. It permits $v=0$ when $D>0$ and otherwise requires $v>v_0$. On this half-line the affine menu numerator is negative somewhere if its slope $drb-J(q)$ is negative, or if its value at $v_0$ is strictly negative. A negative slope permits a finite large rate. For nonnegative slope, the lower endpoint value gives the necessity and, by continuity, suffices even if the endpoint is excluded. For $D<0$, multiplying its value at $v_0$ by $d(a+k)$ and using $rM=Q$ gives the stated scalar form. Finally $J$ is affine in the one common center $q$ and maximization over the compact convex body is exactly the displayed support function. Each alternative is monotone in $J$, since $v_0\ge0$.
statement:
Let full-dimensional convex bodies $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, occupy bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Write $a=|A|$, $k=|K|$, $b=|B|$, $M=a+k+b$. Suppose $Q$ is the old global raw mixed depth maximum and the ordinary raw endpoint maxima satisfy $m_A<Q=m_B$. Let $v_0,\ldots,v_d$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero, $y_0\in\operatorname{int}K$, $s_i^0=v_i\cdot y_0$, and $h_i=h_B(v_i)$. Suppose the ambient caps with thresholds $2s_i^0-h_i,s_i^0,h_i$ have common raw mass $Q$, with all $A$ cuts proper.

Let $A_t,K_t$ be actual convex bodies for small $t\ge0$ converging in Hausdorff distance to $A,K$, with $(A_t+B)/2\subseteq K_t$, $|A_t\mathbin{\triangle} A|+|K_t\mathbin{\triangle} K|=O(t)$, and $|A_t|+|K_t|=a+k+tD+o(t)$. For every fixed $R$, assume uniformly for $|s-s_i^0|\le Rt$ that
$$
|K_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge s\}|+|A_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge 2s-h_i\}|
=Q-(k_i+2\sigma_i)(s-s_i^0)+t\eta_i+o(t),
$$
where $k_i,\sigma_i$ are the old proper section areas on $K,A$ divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Set $\lambda_i=(k_i+2\sigma_i)^{-1}$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $q_{\rm shape}=\sum_i\lambda_i\eta_i/\Lambda$, $r=Q/M$, and $C=q_{\rm shape}-rD$.

For any $q\in B$ and fixed finite $v\ge0$, contract $B$ about $q$ by $1-vt$. Set $J(q)=\sum_i\lambda_i\sigma_i(h_i-v_i\cdot q)/\Lambda$. The resulting family is compatible and has total mass $M+t(D-dbv)+o(t)$. There is a unique nearby equal-budget source $y_t=y_0+O(t)$ at the new $B$ support thresholds. Its common raw cap mass is $Q+t(q_{\rm shape}-vJ(q))+o(t)$ and bounds every middle depth. Its right velocity is determined by $v_i\cdot y'(0+)=[\eta_i-v\sigma_i(h_i-v_i\cdot q)-q_{\rm shape}+vJ(q)]/(k_i+2\sigma_i)$. The new raw maximum at $B_t$ is $(1-vt)^dQ$, and at $A_t$ it stays strictly below $Q$ by a uniform gap. The two initially tied branches of this normalized upper comparison have derivatives with numerators
$$
C+v(drb-J(q)),\qquad -r[D+dv(a+k)],
$$
both divided by $M$.

At a fixed center $q$, this certificate admits strict first-order decrease of both tied branches at some finite $v\ge0$ if and only if
$$
J(q)>drb
\quad\text{or}\quad
C+v_0(drb-J(q))<0,\qquad
v_0=\max\{0,-D/[d(a+k)]\}.
$$
If $D<0$ the second condition is equivalent to $d(a+k)q_{\rm shape}+D J(q)-dQD<0$. If $D\ge0$ it is $C<0$. There exists such a center and rate exactly when the same criterion holds at the attained value
$$
J_{\max}=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i\sigma_i h_i+h_B(-\sum_i\lambda_i\sigma_i v_i)}{\Lambda}.
$$
title: Signed three-fiber variation with one tied endpoint
